features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here, as this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.
Skubal to NYM | Peralta to BAL Sato to CHC | Gray to MIN | Bauers to BOS
The deal: One year, $20 million (includes a $6 million signing bonus and a $16 million player option for 2028 with a $1.5 million buyout) Grade: C+
The Toronto Blue Jays need offense in the worst way and in Jazz Chisholm Jr., they add a veteran lefty swinger with positional versatility to augment the depth chart in several ways.
It's most likely the Blue Jays see him as their new second baseman, pushing Ernie Clement into a utility role, though the righty-swinging Clement might see plenty of time against lefties.

Chisholm is not exactly a take-and-rake hitter, but he's close enough to one that his style is a complement to the Blue Jays' overall profile. Toronto needs power hitting more than anything, and Chisholm is a guy who will trade contact for pop.

A better fit would have been Brandon Lowe, but the Jays already have a lot of committed payroll so maybe Chisholm fits better from that standpoint. While not an elite power hitter, he's an upgrade in that department over Clement.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
Infielder/outfielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. and the Toronto Blue Jays are in agreement on a one-year, $20 million contract with a player option, a source told ESPN.
The Pittsburgh Pirates are sending catcher Henry Davis, the 2021 No. 1 pick, to the Arizona Diamondbacks in exchange for utility player Tim Tawa, sources told ESPN.

Left-handed reliever A.J. Puk and the Washington Nationals are in agreement on a one-year, $5 million contract, sources tell ESPN. Puk can earn $2.5 million in incentives and has a trade kicker as well.
Right-hander Kevin Ginkel and the Minnesota Twins are in agreement on a two-year, $18 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Left-hander Patrick Sandoval and the Colorado Rockies are in agreement on a three-year, $42 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Outfielder Luis Robert Jr. and the Baltimore Orioles are in agreement on a one-year, $12 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Left-hander David Peterson and the Colorado Rockies are in agreement on a two-year, $32 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Right-hander Kevin Gausman and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $25 million contract, pending physical, sources tell ESPN.

features.headline: Would any USMNT players really make Man United better if they followed Poch?
features.desc: Now that USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino has taken over Man United, would it make sense for USMNT players to join their ex-coach?
body: If you follow the U.S. men's national team, here's a good sanity check: Imagine going back in time — say, 15 years — and telling your past self about the current situation.

"Yeah, so there's this guy who came up through the FC Dallas academy, moved to Schalke when he was a kid, started for them as an 18-year-old when they finished second in the Bundesliga behind Bayern Munich, and then moved to Juventus.
He has played more Serie A matches for Juve than anyone else in the seven seasons since he joined the team."

"And he just did this news conference where he said, 'Guys from here being talked about going to Manchester United' was 'inevitable.' Oh, and this is important: he was saying that because Manchester United just poached the USMNT manager in the middle of the Premier League season."

Think about all the assumptions your 15-years-younger self would be making, whenever they had regained consciousness after suffering the double-whammy of learning that time travel exists and that the USMNT was one step below Manchester United in the global pecking order.
... Schalke are one of the best development clubs in the world, and Juventus are one of the best clubs in the world, so one of the best soccer players in the world plays for the USMNT now?

And then, well, the USMNT coach is now coaching Manchester United, which might be the best club in the world. If my math is right, then there was a World Cup a couple of months ago — in summer 2026 — so... wait... did the U.S. just win the World Cup?

features.headline: VAR review: Why Man United should've gotten winner vs. Sporting
features.desc: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
body: The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.
Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship.

With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday.
Referee: Szymon Marciniak VAR: Piotr Lasyk Time: 80 minutes Incident: Sporting's Luis Suárez challenged United goalkeeper Senne Lammens as he attempted to catch a high ball.

The United keeper then dropped the ball under the pressure of Suárez, with the Sporting attacker helping himself to the loose ball and scoring his second goal of the night. The on-field decision was a goal.
VAR Decision: VAR checked and cleared the on-field decision, and the goal stood.
VAR Review: VAR were very comfortable that no offense had been committed by the Sporting attacker and cleared the on-field decision as correct.
Verdict / Insight: It was a correct call by the on-field referee to allow the goal and an equally correct non-intervention from VAR.

features.headline: Superlatives for this MLB free agent class, from Lowe to Gausman
features.desc: Next best move for Mets? Best free agency timing? We have a yearbook's worth of awards for the top MLB free agents.
body: We still have a week left of potential chaos before the expected lockout freezes all moves, so while we still have time, let's dig in to the MLB offseason with our annual free agent superlatives.

Not included: Tarik Skubal, the most superlative in this class. He's headed to the New York Mets, who will pay him, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette about the same as what the Milwaukee Brewers paid for their entire World Series-winning roster in 2026.
In a weak year for position players, the top two are similar-looking outfielders: Suzuki and Randy Arozarena.

Both will be entering their age-32 seasons, are coming off their best seasons (5.1 WAR for Suzuki, 5.7 for Arozarena), hit right-handed, received qualifying offers and are projected to receive four-year, $90 million contracts.

Among the teams possibly looking for a corner outfielder: the Philadelphia Phillies (25th in OPS from their corner outfielders), Baltimore Orioles (26th), Toronto Blue Jays (27th), Houston Astros (30th) and San Diego Padres (17th, but they would move Fernando Tatis Jr. to second base).
The Seattle Mariners might look to replace Arozarena with Suzuki. Which one would you rather have?

First off, given their age, both are risky bets — or, at the minimum, unlikely to repeat those 5-WAR seasons. Check out the number of position players 32 or older who had 4-or-more WAR in recent seasons (with outfielders or DHs in parenthesis):
2026: 5 (Mike Trout) 2025: 9 (Aaron Judge, George Springer, Kyle Schwarber) 2024: 4 (Judge, Marcell Ozuna) 2023: 2 2022: 5 (Springer)

features.headline: Ripple effects of Tarik Skubal signing on Mets, Dodgers and more
features.desc: The impact of the record deal for MLB's top free agent extends past his new team to the top suitors who missed out on him.
body: After finishing 20 games behind the Atlanta Braves and 14 games behind the Philadelphia Phillies in the National League East in 2026, locking up the winter's No. 1 free agent, Tarik Skubal, seemingly pushes the New York Mets closer to the teams that have largely dominated their division this decade.

That will be the case in 2027, anyway. The new collective bargaining agreement rules, whatever they are, might not go into effect until 2028 and beyond — and the Mets' long-term chances for contention could be at risk in the on-going CBA negotiations.
The ripple effects from owner Steve Cohen's $450 million investment in the two-time Cy Young Award winner will not fully take shape until after the labor agreement is concluded.
Sources on the management side report that the owners fully expect to come out of the CBA fight with a salary cap — and will pursue a hard cap on team spending.
Of course, the players will have something to say about that; the MLB Players Association leaders say they'll never agree to a cap.
If MLB's economic system changes significantly, how a contract like Skubal's might fit into the owners' vision is unknown.

The talk among some rival team officials, in the first hours after the agreement, is how much the Mets have at stake in these CBA negotiations — especially if the resulting rules don't allow owners to simply buy their way out of salary restrictions with luxury taxes.
Francisco Lindor's contract runs through 2031 at an average of $34.1 million per season, and Juan Soto's deal is for $51 million annually through 2039. Bo Bichette is set to make $42 million in 2028.
